_about: Revenue-per-slot optimizer settings. FICTIONAL TEACHING BUSINESS: Channel Light Excursions, Juneau. Every price, share and count here is invented for teaching. Keys that start with _ are notes. The tool never changes a price: it writes a memo for the owner.
business: Channel Light Excursions, Juneau (FICTIONAL TEACHING BUSINESS)

operation._allocation_per_day: Fictional glacier commercial-use allocation, guest visits per day. Contractual: check your permit.
operation._seats_per_departure: Fictional vessel limit. Legal mandate: your vessel's Coast Guard certificate of inspection sets it (vessel-specific; confirm the current certificate).
operation._all_aboard_buffer_minutes: Minutes between the return to the dock and the ship's all-aboard time. 0 matches how the fictional 2026 season was actually sold (calibration). The stated plan is 60: see scenario BUFFER60. Policy choice.

COMBO.label: Whale and Glacier Combo
COMBO._price_options_adult: Fictional options to test, not advice. The child price moves in the same proportion as the adult price.

WHALE.label: Whale Only
WHALE._price_options_adult: Fictional options to test, not advice.

channels._net_share: Share of the ticket price the business keeps, by channel. Fictional contracts, not industry norms. Contractual: check your cruise line and OTA agreements.

day_types._how: The kit's day-type rule, the same as tool 3b. Port load = cruise passengers in port / the day's passenger limit (16,000; Saturday 12,000, from the port schedule). Last-season use = the combo's allocation used % on the same weekday in the same month last season. Heavy if port load >= 70% or use >= 95%. Light only if port load < 40% and use < 75% (or no use data). Medium otherwise. Last season's own days use that season's month-and-weekday average. Policy choice: the owner can edit the thresholds. Checked against 2026 use: 2026 heavy days sold 98.1 of 100 combo slots on average, light days 49.2.

uncertainty._label: Assumptions, not measurements. The fictional business has never tested a price change and has one season of data. Wide ranges on purpose. Replace them with your own evidence.
uncertainty._price_elasticity: Percent change in requests for a 1 percent price change. Mid -1.0 is a neutral starting point: away from the cap, a price change neither gains nor loses revenue in the middle case, so the model does not build in a bias for or against raising prices.
uncertainty._steer_acceptance: Share of independent (OTA and direct) parties who take the departure you offer first when you steer them away from the times ships need.

operating_options.label: As 2026: first come, any time that fits
Protect combo seats from whale-only until the release point
Offer independents the departures ships use least
Protect combo seats and steer independents

rules._protect_release_share: Protection stops after this share of a day's requests has arrived (the last 10 percent book after the release, for example inside 48 hours). Assumption.
rules._cap_day_margin: A day counts as 'at the cap' when 5 or fewer slots are left, as in summary_2026.json.

monte_carlo._how: Each draw picks a demand level (the same percentile for every day type: a bad season is bad everywhere), a price response and a whale-only acceptance from the ranges above. The same draws are used for every option (common random numbers), so differences between options are not noise from different draws.

decision_rule._how: Policy choice. For each day type, a change from the 2026 settings is recommended only if it earns more than keeping them in at least min_win_share of draws, each changed lever (combo price, whale-only price, operating option) also does so on its own, and the median gain is at least min_median_gain dollars. Among those, the highest median wins. season_net counts combo and whale-only net revenue; per_slot counts combo only (Number 4).

scenarios.label: Keep the stated 60-minute return buffer before all-aboard
scenarios._assumptions: Same demand and settings as the recommended plan. Cruise parties only book departures that return 60 minutes before all-aboard. Policy choice: guest safety margin versus seats.

scenarios.label: Add an 11:45 departure on heavy days (a second vessel, 30 seats)
scenarios._assumptions: A second vessel, crew and shuttle seats are available at 11:45 on heavy days. The glacier allocation does not change, so the combo stays capped at 100 a day: on days at or near the cap most added seats can only sell whale-only. Costs (charter, crew hours, fuel, shuttle) are NOT modeled: compare the gain with your own cost before deciding.

scenarios.label: Add an 11:45 departure on medium days (a second vessel, 30 seats)
scenarios._assumptions: Same as the heavy-day scenario, on medium days instead. These days are mostly below the cap, so seats at a time that fits the ships can win back combo guests. Costs are NOT modeled.

demand._how: Calibrated by 'python optimize.py --calibrate' from last season's files. Requests = sold + turned away (both causes) + estimated whale-only converts at the cap. Fitted line: requests = per_1000_passengers x passengers in port / 1000 + month base. Low and high per day type combine the whale-only acceptance range, the change-versus-last-season assumption and the fit's uncertainty. Edit the ranges if you know more; rerun --calibrate to rebuild them from data.
